label: Article 115, Swiss Criminal Code
description: Assisting suicide is punishable only when done for selfish motives. There is no dedicated assisted dying law: everything else rests on this one clause, in force since the 1940s.

label: Narcotics law (BetmG)
description: Sodium pentobarbital is listed as a narcotic. It may only be dispensed on a prescription from a doctor or vet: where the legislature stayed silent on assisted dying, narcotics law does the governing.
source: University of Zurich, commentary on BGE 133 I 58

label: Therapeutic Products Act (HMG)
description: Medicines law, applied alongside the narcotics law to pentobarbital. Doctors have been prosecuted under it for prescribing to people who wanted to die.

label: Federal Supreme Court, BGE 133 I 58 (2006)
description: No right to obtain pentobarbital without a prescription, and no constitutional duty for the state to provide it. The ruling that made the prescription the door.

label: Federal Supreme Court, 2C_839/2008 (2009)
description: Dignitas was refused its own authorisation to obtain, hold and dispense pentobarbital, including a reserve stock.

label: Beck rulings (2021, 2024)
description: A Geneva doctor prescribed pentobarbital to a healthy 86-year-old woman who wanted to die with her husband. The Federal Supreme Court found no breach of medicines law (2021) or narcotics law (2024): giving the drug to a healthy person is an ethical question, not a medical one.

label: Preisig cases (2019 to 2023)
description: A Basel-Landschaft doctor helped a mentally ill woman die without an independent psychiatric assessment. Acquitted of homicide; first convicted for medicine violations, later acquitted by the Federal Supreme Court. The case also involved unlabelled doses obtained and stored.
source: SRF; Federal Supreme Court press release, 6B_1087/2021

label: Article 253, Criminal Procedure Code
description: Every assisted suicide is an extraordinary death (aussergewöhnlicher Todesfall) that must be reported and examined. Switzerland reviews each death after it happens, as a possible crime, then closes the file.

label: Basel-Landschaft police checklist
description: What police verify after each assisted suicide: identity, the signed declaration, a prescription copy under six months old, the collection authorisation, the death protocol with infusion report, self-administration, and that prescription and container match.

label: Institute of Forensic Medicine, Basel
description: Notified after each assisted suicide in the region; may examine the scene and the medical documents.

label: Cantonal prosecutors
description: Informed of every assisted suicide; in Basel-Landschaft such cases usually end with a decision not to open proceedings. They also prosecuted the Preisig and Sarco cases.

label: Swissmedic
description: The medicines agency. It refused Dignitas a licence to hold pentobarbital and has called it delicate when one person holds several roles in a case.

label: Cantonal pharmacists' position paper
description: Guidance from the cantonal pharmacists on how pentobarbital should be dispensed for assisted suicide. Known only through a trade article so far.
verification_note: The paper itself has not been read yet.

label: Federal Parliament
description: Rejected framework legislation on assisted suicide in 2025 and favoured monitoring instead; earlier rejected a motion to count assisted-suicide tourism.

label: Federal Statistical Office
description: Counts assisted suicides among residents only: 1,729 in 2023. People who travel to Switzerland to die are not in the official figures, though the office says it is considering counting them.

label: SAMW guidelines, adopted by the FMH (2022)
description: Professional ethics binding FMH doctors: assisted suicide for healthy people is not ethically justifiable; at least two detailed discussions, two weeks apart. Organisations protested.

label: Prescribing doctors
description: The doorkeepers. They assess capacity and diagnosis and write the prescription; when a person's own doctor refuses, organisations refer them to doctors they work with.
verification_note: Who they are and how many prescriptions each writes is an open question.

label: Compounding pharmacies
description: There are no finished tablets: pharmacies obtain the substance from specialised suppliers and prepare it. Any pharmacy may dispense on a valid prescription; none is obliged to, and some have refused.

label: The lethal solution
description: Pentobarbital dissolved in water and drunk, injected through a stomach tube, or run through an intravenous line the person opens themselves, usually after an antiemetic. Sleep follows within minutes.

label: Companions (Freitodbegleiter)
description: Organisation staff who bring the drug at the agreed time and stay present. EXIT also employs on-call infusion specialists.

label: Raw substance suppliers
description: Industry directories list Siegfried, founded in Zofingen, among pentobarbital sodium suppliers.
verification_note: A directory listing does not establish Swiss production or that it supplies Swiss pharmacies.

label: EXIT (Deutsche Schweiz)
description: Founded 1982, Zurich. The largest organisation: 1,421 deaths in 2025, nearly 196,000 members. Swiss citizens and residents only; free after three years of membership.

label: EXIT A.D.M.D. Suisse romande
description: Founded 1982, Geneva. Residents only; 502 deaths in 2022. Historically more restrictive on psychiatric cases.

label: Dignitas
description: Founded 1998 after a split at EXIT. Accepts members from abroad; a house in canton Zurich since 2009. 250 deaths in 2023.

label: The provisional green light
description: Dignitas's step when a doctor agrees in principle to prescribe. Its founder claimed 70% of those who get it never come back: the prescription as possibility rather than means.
verification_note: The 70% is the founder's own claim.
source: PBS Frontline, interview with Ludwig Minelli

label: Lifecircle / Eternal Spirit
description: Twin bodies founded by Erika Preisig after she left Dignitas in 2010; deaths took place in an apartment in Basel. No new members since 2022.

label: Pegasos
description: Founded in Basel in 2019. No incurable illness required; around CHF 10,000. An estimated 200 to 300 deaths a year, mostly foreigners; repeated controversy over families not told.

label: Athanasios
description: Founded in 2025 in Basel-Landschaft by a former nurse; his team reportedly handled almost 250 foreign cases the year before. One of four new organisations for foreigners.

label: Ex International
description: A small organisation founded in 1996 in Bern that also accepts foreigners.

label: Sarco capsule
description: A capsule that replaces oxygen with nitrogen, first used in September 2024 in Schaffhausen and presented as a drug-free death. Several arrests followed: a death without pentobarbital became a police matter.

label: Philip Nitschke / Exit International
description: Australian right-to-die activist behind the Sarco. Allied with Pegasos, then broke with it; his late-2025 guide names Athanasios as his new go-to organisation.

label: Assisted-suicide tourism
description: People travelling to Switzerland to die, mostly through small organisations in the Basel and Zurich regions. A recurring public controversy, and invisible in the official statistics.

label: Families not told
description: Press coverage, mostly British, of people who died with Pegasos without their families knowing, including a Welsh woman in January 2025.

label: Care homes and hospitals
description: Whether institutions must admit assisted suicide organisations. EXIT campaigns for access; in 2023 EXIT romande led a referendum in Geneva against repealing the obligation.

label: Illicit online offers
description: Spam posts offering 'Swiss' pentobarbital without prescription. Recorded only as discourse: in black-market talk, Switzerland works as a guarantee of quality.

label: Jox et al. 2024
description: Assisted suicide in Switzerland, 1999 to 2022: from 63 cases to almost 1,600, 2.1% of deaths.

label: Rütsche, Hürlimann & Thommen 2022
description: Legal analysis of whether assisting healthy people with pentobarbital is punishable.

label: Deutsches Ärzteblatt Int. 2019
description: Overview of assisted suicide in Switzerland, including the organisations providing it.

label: Jolicorps 2007
description: Master's ethnography of EXIT A.D.M.D.: medicalisation as the tool that legitimised assisted suicide.

label: Stavrianakis 2020
description: Leaving: A Narrative of Assisted Suicide. An anthropological account of assisted suicide in Switzerland.
verification_note: Not yet read; check its field site and organisation.

label: MORTALMED
description: ERC project led by Marcos Freire de Andrade Neves; this map prepares fieldwork for the subproject Lethal Prescriptions, with fieldwork in Basel.
